title: MEMORY
subtitle: Wearable AI Context Engine
oneLiner: An experimental ambient wearable AI that passively captures, indexes, and structures real-world dialogue in real time.
description: MEMORY explores how ambient computing can serve as an external cognitive buffer. Processing continuous audio on local edge hardware, it detects voice activity, transcribes speech locally, and structures conceptual relationships into a private vector graph without relying on third-party cloud infrastructure.
highlights: Low-power dual MEMS microphone capture paired with edge companion board
Real-time voice activity detection pruning silence before neural inference
Local quantized Whisper model generating millisecond-stamped transcripts
Embedded vector database mapping personal concept associations
takeaway: Quantization and deliberate data pruning matter more than raw compute when deploying intelligence to the physical edge.

title: VEYR
subtitle: Autonomous Generative Mythology
oneLiner: An original dark mythology and procedural worldbuilding engine generating interconnected folklore and artifacts.
description: VEYR investigates whether a computational pipeline can construct a coherent mythological canon with its own linguistic grammar, pantheon genealogies, and visual artifacts. Using chained latent diffusion models and directed acyclic graph lore trees, it generates an evolving fictional civilization.
highlights: Directed acyclic graph defining metaphysical axioms and historical factions
LLM arbitration resolving faction conflicts based on canonical philosophy
Diffusion pipelines synthesizing consistent architectural monoliths and glyphs
Interactive cosmological viewport exploring generational lore timelines
takeaway: Generative systems produce artistic resonance only when bounded by rigid architectural axioms.

title: THE LAST RADIO
subtitle: Narrative Audio Simulation
oneLiner: A psychological simulation built around tactile radio frequency modulation, audio decay, and atmospheric bounce.
description: Set in a silent, post-collapse world where the only remaining human contact occurs through electromagnetic frequency drift. Players tune an analog heterodyne receiver through static, harmonic interference, and atmospheric bounce to decipher fragmented transmissions, voice logs, and emergency broadcasts.
highlights: Custom heterodyne tuning DSP simulating authentic analog drift and carrier whine
Dynamic ionospheric propagation calculations altering reception based on virtual weather
Procedural acoustic decay and tape hiss rendering via Web Audio buffers
Minimalist phosphor oscilloscope visualizer reacting to audio amplitude
takeaway: Sound creates deeper emotional immersion than photorealistic graphics when designed with tactile physics.

title: AEGIS // KERNEL PROBE
subtitle: eBPF Adversarial Detection Runtime
oneLiner: A lightweight Linux security daemon leveraging eBPF kprobes to observe system calls and detect anomalous execution.
description: AEGIS attaches non-blocking eBPF kprobes directly to Linux kernel syscalls (execve, openat, connect) to construct a real-time behavioral graph of active processes. By analyzing execution patterns against known baseline behavior, it detects code injection and privilege escalation with near-zero latency.
highlights: Zero-overhead syscall telemetry collected inside kernel space via BPF programs
Ring-buffer IPC streaming anomalous process identifiers to user-space daemon
Heuristic scoring engine catching reflective memory payloads without file touching
Automated socket teardown and namespace isolation on critical violation
takeaway: True security cannot be bolted on at the application layer; it must live in the kernel execution path.
